messages:
olivia: Heads up - support ticket: hovercard shows negative cache savings for low-traffic route after sampling change. Example: route=/chat-stream model=redwood-3b sample_rate=0.003 -> -$0.06
maria: yep that's warmup amortization vs noisy hit-rate. small-n problem.
rajiv: agree. current API returns a single number which is misleading. we should include sample_count and a CI or fallback to rollup.
ben: quick proposal: backend v2 returns {estimate, sample_count, ci_low, ci_high, source}. source ∈ [live, rollup, suppressed]. header X-Rollup-Used when rollup chosen.
sophie: UX: show "n=XX" and "95% CI" under the number. if source==rollup show a clock icon and "24h rollup" tooltip. if suppressed show "insufficient samples" with CTA: "view 7d rollup"
maria: thresholds: ROLLUP_MIN=30, LIVE_MIN=100 default. make org-configurable. also need feature flag for ?force_live_estimate (audited).
ben: backend picks analytic CI via delta-method for common routes; fallback to precomputed bootstrap from daily rollup for high-variance ones. precompute to avoid live CPU cost.
rajiv: also surface a small banner when tenant throttle_rate > 0.2: "quota may be limiting samples" so SREs don't get misled.
olivia: sounds good. can we log hover_request events: {chain, route, source, sample_count, user_forced}? want to measure how often rollup hides anomalies.
ben: will add hover_request + force_live_click telemetry. I'll open PR feat/hover-stats-v2 and include mock payloads.
maria: pls post mock payload here so QA can validate against the ticketed tenant.
deploy-bot: deploybot: scheduled canary deploy telemetry-hover-v2 in 12m :rocket:
olivia: thanks team — this should cut down on support noise. I'll follow up after canary validation.
